Unofficial integration, not affiliated with everHome. It reads an
**EcoTracker**, the everHome optical reader clipped on the infrared port of
an electricity meter, through its local API: no cloud, no account, nothing
sent to the reader but one read (`GET /v1/json`) every 10 seconds.

**Never tested with a real EcoTracker**: the integration was written from
the maker's Python library (everhome-gmbh/ecotracker) and the published
description of its local API. Your feedback is welcome.

## What you get

One **EcoTracker** device (or **EcoTracker \<serial number>** when the reader
gives one), with the values the meter gives (a meter sends only some of
them):

| Feature                                    | Kind                     | Field of the reader            |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| Net power (negative when the home injects) | energy sensor, W         | `power`                        |
| Consumption index                          | energy index, kWh        | `energyCounterIn`              |
| Consumption index, tariffs 1 and 2 (kWh)   | plain sensor             | `energyCounterInT1`, `…T2`     |
| Injection index (kWh)                      | plain sensor             | `energyCounterOut`             |
| Net power, average of the last minute      | plain sensor, W          | `powerAvg`                     |
| Power L1, L2, L3 (W)                       | plain sensor, no history | `powerPhase1` to `powerPhase3` |
| Wi-Fi signal (dBm)                         | plain sensor, no history | `rssi` (when given)            |

- The **consumption index** feeds the Gladys energy monitoring, which
  derives the consumption and its cost from it. It is published once a
  minute and checked first: never 0; any drop, even of 1 Wh, or a jump the
  home could not have drawn (more than 50 kW on average) is **held back**
  (the last accepted value is sent again), kept across restarts and shown in
  the status of the integration. Neither time nor repetition confirms it.
- The **injection** and the **tariffs** never enter the energy monitoring
  (the injection would be billed as consumption, the tariffs counted twice):
  plain sensors.
- `energyCounterIn` and `energyCounterOut` are in Wh according to the
  published API description and a real answer: they are converted to kWh.
  For T1 and T2 the description gives no unit: Wh is an assumption (its
  example has In = T1 + T2). The README of the maker's library says kWh: the
  integration therefore checks the unit. When the index does not follow the
  power (its rise is outside 1/20 to 20 times the energy the power gives,
  over at least 1 kWh), or when T1 + T2 do not make the index, the status
  says so ("unit?"); the index is still sent.
- The powers are sent every 10 seconds, only when they change (and every
  10 minutes otherwise). They are not sent:
  - when the reader says (field `agePower`) that its power is more than a
    minute old;
  - when no value read (powers, counters) has moved for 15 minutes: the
    reader may serve an old reading (optical head moved); a meter at rest may
    too, the status says so;
  - after a start, until the reading moves (about ten seconds), unless
    `agePower` says it is recent: a reading frozen before a restart is not
    sent as new.

  The index goes on in all these cases.

- When the meter later gives new values (meter unlocked with its PIN), the
  device gets new features: in the **Discover** tab, click **Update** on the
  device to add them (its history is kept).

## Setup

1. Install the EcoTracker on your meter and connect it to your Wi-Fi with the
   everHome app, as the maker explains. If the app offers it, turn on the
   local API of the reader.
2. Find its IP address (in your router or the app) and give it a fixed
   address in your router (DHCP reservation). It is needed when the reader
   gives no serial number (see below).
3. In Gladys, open the integration, enter this address, save.
4. In the **Discover** tab, create the device.

If the status says the meter gives no power, it is probably PIN-locked:
enter on the meter the PIN given by your grid operator to unlock its
extended data. The indexes go on meanwhile. When the reader gives no serial
number and you take it off the meter to enter the PIN, it then answers with
new fields after an outage: all its values, the index included, are held
(the status says so). Two clicks on **Accept the held index** lift it.

## Buttons

- **Test the connection**: reads the reader when a read is due (never more
  than one every 10 seconds), otherwise tells the last read.
- **Accept the held index**, in two clicks, only when the held value is right
  (new meter, long outage):
  - the first click shows the movement held (a jump or a drop) and accepts
    nothing;
  - the second click, from 3 seconds to 5 minutes later, takes that value,
    plus what the meter may have measured between the two clicks (at most
    4.667 kWh);
  - when the held value changed otherwise between the clicks (another
    direction, another starting point, a larger jump), nothing is taken: look
    at the status and start again.

  An accepted jump is counted at once as consumption; an accepted drop bills
  nothing, the consumption goes on from there. Saving the configuration never
  accepts anything.

  The same button, in two clicks, also accepts the **new fields** of a
  reader without serial number after an outage (see "Identity of the
  reader"): the first click shows them, the second keeps them; the index
  stays checked by its guard.

## Identity of the reader

- The real reader we know gives no serial number in its local answer: the
  device is then named **EcoTracker** (`ecotracker:reader`), and another
  reader answering at the same address (a second EcoTracker of the home
  taking its address) cannot always be told from it. A **fixed address is
  therefore needed**. What still protects:
  - after an outage (reader unreachable, restart), an answer whose meter
    fields differ (powers, phases, counters and tariffs; not `agePower`,
    `rssi`, `firmwareVersion`, which belong to the reader) is not used: nothing is sent until
    the fields come back, or until two clicks on **Accept the held index** if
    it is the same reader;
  - with the same fields, the guard of the index holds a drop, or a rise
    larger than the home could have drawn since the last accepted value
    (50 kW × hours without values); **a smaller rise is taken as
    consumption** (after a 2-hour outage, up to 100 kWh).
- When the reader gives a serial number (field `serial`, read by the maker's
  library), the device carries it and every answer is checked: another
  number at the same address gets its own device, its values never go to the
  previous one; an unreadable number is not used (red status, new try
  spaced out).
- An answer without number is not used while a device of a reader with a
  number exists in Gladys: the status says so. If you replaced the
  reader with one without number, delete the old device in Gladys: the new
  reader then gets its own device.
- Going from a reader without number to one with a number (after an update
  of the reader, for instance) creates a new device, without the history of
  the old one.

## Limits

- One reader per integration.
- An unreadable counter (text, negative value, 0, out of bounds) is never
  used. The status says so for the consumption counter (`energyCounterIn`);
  unreadable tariffs and injection are simply ignored.
- Read-only: the reader receives no command.

## Troubleshooting

The status of the integration says what is going on: missing or invalid
address, unreachable reader or unexpected answer (new try after 10 s, doubled
up to 5 minutes), reader asking to wait (HTTP 429 or 5xx: reads paused from
1 minute to 6 hours, kept across a restart), index held back, old values. To
look at the reader yourself, open `http://<address>/v1/json` in a browser on
the same network.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt EcoTracker in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EcoTracker | `section` | Nein | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with everHome. It reads your EcoTracker, the optical reader clipped on the infrared port of an electricity meter, through its local API (to turn on in the everHome app if it offers it), without any cloud: the net power every 10 seconds, the consumption index every minute for the Gladys energy monitoring, and, when the reader gives them, the tariff counters and the injection as plain sensors, the average power, the power per phase. Read-only. Never tested with a real EcoTracker. |
| EcoTracker address | `string` | Ja | The IP address of the EcoTracker on your network (shown by your router or the everHome app), with a port only if it is not 80. Give it a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation): it is needed when the reader gives no serial number, since another device taking its address could not always be told from it. If the address changes, enter the new one: the device and its history are kept. |

## So installierst du EcoTracker in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: EcoTracker erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-ecotracker:0.1.2`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecotracker](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecotracker).

EcoTracker benötigt Gladys `>=5.2.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

EcoTracker ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
